A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same three-step ICL circuit study. All 31 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Retained content can be matched across renaming, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original representation measurements, attention-head analyses, classification and ablation results on Llama and Falcon models, plus Pythia pretraining-checkpoint experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds token-copying comparisons, missing-correct-label experiments and a named-person classification counterexample.

M1.justification: The three inference stages, head-identification criteria and decoding/bypass procedures remain unchanged. 'Summarize' becomes 'Input Text Encode.' The new copying and output-divergence measures diagnose the existing circuit rather than modify its operation.

E1.justification: The six sentence-classification datasets remain. Appendix G adds targeted evaluation of contexts omitting the correct query label and a small occupation-classification case using Geoffrey Hinton and Michael Jordan, extending the represented scenarios and input types.

E2.justification: Figure 19 adds a random baseline to the new comparison between attention-derived predictions and model outputs. Existing ablation and decoding comparator sets are retained. The newly discussed gradient-descent and Bayesian explanations are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols measure length-normalized preceding-token attention and Jensen–Shannon divergence, selecting the five lowest-divergence heads per layer. Appendix G also filters contexts by correct-label absence. Existing default sampling, model settings and ablation-layer fractions remain unchanged; Appendix A.7 chiefly clarifies the existing intervention.

E4.justification: Appendix D newly tests whether copying differs between label and non-label positions. Appendix G adds explanatory-fidelity comparisons, circuit ablations when the correct label is absent, and a counterexample where demonstrations help despite weak induction activity. These substantially extend the tests of the circuit's mechanism and applicability.

E5.justification: Random-ablation controls in Table 1 and v1 Table 6/v2 Table 8 change from single reported values to mean ± standard deviation. Repetition counts and seeds remain unspecified, so the PDFs establish new uncertainty reporting but not an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: Original target-ablation scores remain, but control values change: Table 1's 75% demonstration-encoding control moves from -4.65 to -3.29 ± 1.87. New Table 6 reports +22.95 and +29.26 percentage points from full Step 3 ablation under missing-label conditions for Llama 3 8B and Falcon 7B. Copying distributions, divergence results and occupation-label probabilities are also added. These are new-condition findings, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendices D and G.1 introduce mathematical definitions for normalized copy magnitude and an attention-derived label distribution, Equations 15–17. The earlier kernel-alignment derivation, centroid rules and hidden-space argument are retained. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the three-stage explanation, dominance claim and parallel bypasses. Section 6 adds an explicit priority claim that this is the first work to unify fragmented empirical conclusions, strengthening the stated novelty of the retained contribution.

C2.justification: V2 substantially develops the circuit's applicability boundary: induction can harm prediction when the correct label is absent, while demonstrations can help through other dynamics. Section 6 expressly qualifies generalization to these cases. V2 also interprets copying as general pretrained behavior and discusses future control through forerunner-token design.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.7 explicitly describes zeroing designated connections and matching random controls within the same layers, supported by Figure 10. Appendix G supplies diagnostic-selection rules and the counterexample prompt. Existing quantization, prompt templates and the promise to release code after acceptance are retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds specific contrasts with gradient-descent, kernel-regression, Bayesian and earlier induction-circuit explanations. Appendix G challenges Wang et al.'s label-anchor interpretation and introduces Xiao et al.'s attention-sink work. Most other reference edits add URLs or update metadata; Xie's 2021 and 2022 entries describe the same work.

P1.justification: V2 makes local wording corrections, renames Step 1 and clarifies attention-arrow notation. It expands the discussion, inserts appendix sections, and moves the reproducibility, authorship and acknowledgment statements before the references. The main narrative and most existing prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds an ablation schematic, copying and divergence distribution plots, counterexample heatmaps, and two result tables (Figures 10, 15, 19, 20; Tables 6–7). Tables 1 and 8 are widened and reformatted for uncertainty reporting. Earlier plots are retained, with caption, placement and numbering changes.

improvement.justification: The missing-label ablations and explicit counterexample improve scrutiny of the explanation and motivate a clearer applicability limit. Appendix A.7 and control standard deviations improve transparency. These gains are tempered by unspecified repetition counts and reporting errors, including Table 6's duplicated Llama 3 Step 2/Step 3 connection label.
